1. Accused persons are facing trial in this case on allegations of causing simple hurt and uttering abuses on complainant Hansika (PW1) and additionally accused Ram Prasad is facing trial on allegations that he assaulted son of complainant with intention that if, he caused his death then accused would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Brief Facts 2.

Briefly stated the case of prosecution is that on on 07.10.2013, on the receipt of DD No. 16 A, (Ex.
PW11/I) ASI Satyavir Singh, along with Ct Sunil reached at the spot that is NSS-6, Mianwali Nagar,
New Delhi, where complainant Hansika @ Jyoti was found sitting in the PCR van with her two year old son.
PCR, took them to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Mangalpuri.
3. Son of complainant got treated in the Hospital.
Thereafter complainant Hansika came to PS Pachim Vihar West, and gave a written complaint to ASI Satyavir.

English translation of statement of complainant reads as under:
SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
.....

Sir, my request is that today when I went to my in-laws' house at 11.30 am, my in-laws namely Ram Prasad, Shivlal, Mithun Bharti, Rekha, Gumpi, Dipankar, Shiva,
Rohit and Kamla, all of them beaten and abused me.

My child, who is 2 years old, was picked up and thrown by my Chacha father-in-law and his head got injured and I,
Hansinka alias Jyoti was beaten by my in-laws and the entire family.
I request you to register my report and get me justice.
Name of my chacha father-in-law is Ram Prasad who picked up my child Nischal and threw him....
4. On the basis of MLCs of complainant and her son and on the complaint of the complainant FIR under section 323/308/509/34 IPC was registered.
During the investigations, ASI prepared site plan of the place of occurrence.
He recorded statements of witnesses under section 161 CrPC and after arresting the accused persons filed the charge-sheet.
5. During the course of trial accused Shiv Lal unfortunately got expired and the case against him stands abated vide orders dated 06.03.2017.
6. On 10.09.2015 charge for the offence punishable under Section 323/509/34 IPC was framed against all accused persons.

Additionally, accused Ram Prasad has been charged for the offence State vs Shiv Lal Etc on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27293229/
2 punishable under Section 308 IPC.

In their statements recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C, accused persons stated that the alleged incident did not happen and due to matrimonial dispute between the complainant and her husband,
Mithun accused persons have been falsely implicated by complainant.
Defense Evidence 9.
In their defense, accused persons examined DW1 Madan Lal, who produced a CCTV footage of the outside of the place of occurrence and the photographs of it.
DW1 deposed that on the date of incident, he went to house of accused persons to invite them for the lagan ceremony of his son and his son Naveen (DW2) was also along with him.

When they reached in front of the house of accused persons, complainant was present there with her son but he did not notice any blood stain or injury on the head or any part of son of the complainant.
He noticed that the son was playing in the stairs.
DW1 deposed that in his presence police came and complainant along with her son left the house of accused persons with the police officers.

10.
DW2 Naveen Bharti also deposed on the similar lines and testified that when he went to the house of accused persons, he saw complainant was sitting on the stairs with her son.
He also deposed that in his presence, police came at the spot and complainant and her son went along with the police, and at the time there was no injury on their person.
Arguments 11.

Sh. Pankaj Bhatia, Ld Addl. PP for State submitted that complainant has duly supported prosecution case in respect of the incident that she was mercilessly beaten by accused persons and her son was thrown by accused Ram Prasad which resulted into the head injury to the minor son of the complainant.
It is further contended that the medical evidence brought on record corroborates the version of complainant that she along with her son were assaulted by the accused persons.

Thus,
it is submitted that the case of the prosecution in the light of trustworthy evidence of the complainant and medical evidence on record, stands proved against accused persons and as such they are liable to be convicted for the offences they have been charged with.
12.
On the other hand, it is contended on behalf of accused persons that the complainant has set up a totally false case due to her matrimonial dispute with her husband accused Mithun Bharti.
It is stated that no such incident as narrated by the complainant happened.

SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
13.
It is submitted that in the CCTV footage on the incident, complainant can be seen sitting comfortably with her son and going with police officials.
It is stated that deposition of the complainant is marked improvement to her initial complaint.
It is further submitted that the medical evidence on record does not correspond to the version of the complainant.

It is submitted State vs Shiv Lal Etc on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27293229/
4 that the prosecution story is far from truth, and in view of the unreliable evidence of the complainant, accused persons are entitled to be acquitted in the present case.
14.
I have heard Ld. Addl. PP for State and Ld. defense counsel at length.
I have perused the material on record.
Analysis and Discussion 15.
Allegations of Assault (308/323 IPC):

As per prosecution story, on 06.10.2013 at about 1130 AM,
complainant who was residing in her parental house went to her matrimonial home at NS-6, Top Floor, Mianwali Nagar and there she was assaulted by all accused persons who are her in-laws.

In her examination-in-chief, PW1/ complainant deposed as under:
" .......

On 06.10.2013 as per the oral direction of the court of Ms. Anu Malhotra, Ld.
District & Sessions Judge, West in case u/s 498A/406/34 IPC, I along with my son had gone to my matrimonial home.
I reached there at about 11:00/12:00 noon.
I rang the bell of the house.
My parental uncle(Chacha sasur) accused Ram Prasad, who resides there at the top floor, opened the door.

As soon as he saw me, he SC No.
56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
started beating me.
In the meantime my Chachi Saas/accused Rekha also came there and started beating me.

Thereafter, I as soon as I entered the lobby of the house, my mother-in-law and all other accused persons namely Shiva, Rohit, Deepankar and Ritesh and my husband Mithun and father-in-law Shiv Lal started beating me.
They all dragged me out of the house.
My Chacha sasur accused Ram Prasad after slapping me, pushed me out of the house.
Accused Rekha twisted my hands and slapped me and the remaining accused persons caught hold of me from my hair and they all had beaten me by fist and kick blows.
At that time my son Nishal was two years of age.
Accused Ram Prasad had thrown my son against the wall of bathroom saying that "TU ISPE JYADA FOOLTI HAI, LE ISKO HI KHATAM KAR DETA HOON, NA YE HOGA NA TU IDHAR AAYEGI".
I was thrown out of the house.
I made a telephonic call to police.
Accused persons also called the police.
PCR van reached the spot.
Police took me to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital where me and my son were medically examined.

Thereafter after discharge from the hospital, I had given a written complaint in the police station, which is now Ex.PW1/A bearing my signature at point A. ...... "
16.
Complainant in her cross-examination deposed that prior to registration of this case, she had already lodged a case FIR No. 67/13 under section 498A/406/34IPC PS Mianwali Nagar.
thus, it is evident that the relationship between complainant and her husband/in-laws was not cordial and complainant had already registered a case against them.

17. Complainant deposed that on the date of incident, complainant went to her matrimonial home and when she SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
reached there, she was assaulted by accused persons.

Complainant categorically alleged that accused Ram Prasad threw her son against the wall of the bathroom by State vs Shiv Lal Etc on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27293229/
5
saying that "tu ispe jyada foolti hai, le isko hi khatam kar deta hoon, na ye hoga na tu idhar aayegi" and then she was thrown out of the house.
Complainant deposed that she made a telephonic call to the police and accused persons also called the police.

18. The above deposition of complainant is marked improvement to her initial Complaint Ex.
PW1/A in which complainant did not attribute any utterance to accused Ram Prasad, rather, she only stated that accused Ram Prasad thrown her son due to which the he sustained head injury.
19. As deposed by the complainant that her son was thrown against the wall of the bathroom, it was not a minor incident.
Not only a two year old son of a mother was thrown but thrown with an intention to kill that infant, but in her initial complaint, complainant did not mention these facts.
Had this incident have happened, the complainant would have mentioned these facts in the initial complaint but it is not the case here.

20. Facts reveal that complainant was acquainted with process of law as she had already lodged a FIR against the accused persons, as such it is expected from a mother to alt- laest mention in her hand written complaint that accused SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
ram Prasad attempted to kill her son but she did not mention any such fact.
Therefore, the variation between the initial complaint of the complaint, Ex. PW1/A and her deposition is denting the veracity of her version.
21. If we go through the MLC (Ex PW9/A) of minor son of the complainant, it does not mention at all that the he was thrown against a wall.
Had it been so, the complainant would have certainly mentioned this fact to the Doctor attending the child, but she didn't do so.
22. As far as the injuries to the complainant are concerned, it is evident from her MLC Ex PW8/A that she was examined by the Doctor, at about 3:45 PM whereas her son was examined at 12:30 PM.
There is difference of about 3:30 Hours between the medical examination of complainant and her son.
23. As per deposition of complainant, she was beaten by all the accused persons, dragged out of the house by them, her hair were pulled and she was beaten by fist and kick blows.

In such a scenario,
complaint would have suffered some serious injury but after reaching the hospital, she did not get her examined by the Doctor and why she did not to so is not explained.
Injuries sustained by complainant and her son are opined to be simple in nature.
None of the injuries co-relate to the version of incident narrated by the complainant.

SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
24.

In defence, accused persons of examined DW1 Madan Pal & DW2 Naveen Bharti. who deposed that when they reached at the matrimonial house of the complainant, they noticed complainant and her son were sitting on the staircase and then going with the police officers.

Photographs of the CCTV footage are produced on record as Ex. DW1/A and CD of the CCTV footage of relevant date State vs Shiv Lal Etc on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27293229/
6 and time as Ex. DW1/B.
25.
Accused Mithun Bharti examined himself as DW3.

He proved CCTV footage in a DVD Ex.
DW1/B and a certificate Ex DW3/D under Section 65B Indian evidence Act in support of digital record of footage.

He also proved certified copy of judgment filed by him against complainant as Ex.
DW3/A and a copy of FIR no. 67/2013 PS Mianwali Nagar registered on the complaint of complainant as Ex. DW3/B.
26.
CCTV footage shows that at about 11:49 am, complainant pressing the door bell of the house of the accused persons and within a minute she was pushed outside.
Thereafter, complainant and her son are seen sitting on the staircase of the house.
Son of complainant is seen standing at some distance from the complainant.

Had the minor son of the complainant was thrown in the manner complainant described in her evidence, then she would have been attending that minor son and not sitting on the staircase while making her son to stand at a distance.

Complainant SC No.
56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
did not take any measure to immediately rush to a Doctor which indicates that neither she nor minor suffered any injury.
27. Deposition of complainant is not conclusive to hold that accused persons were responsible in causing injuries to her.
There is material inconsistency in her deposition which has actually blurred the exact sequence of events.
PW1 deposed that she did not hand over her blood stained clothes to IO.
It is hardly believable that if at all complainant was wearing blood stained clothes, then why Investigating Agency did not seize those clothes then and there.
It is not in the testimony of HC Sunil who reached at the spot and at hospital with IO that he noticed PW1 wearing blood stained clothes.

28. In Suraj Mal versus The State (Delhi Admn.), AIR 1979 S.C. 1408, it has been observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court:
"Where witness make two inconsistent statements in their evidence either at one stage or at two stages, the testimony of such witnesses becomes unreliable and unworthy of credence and in the absence of special circumstances no conviction can be based on the evidence of such witness."
29.

sentences.text: As narrated above testimony of PW1 is wavering.
She has given different versions of the incident.
It is evident that at different stages of investigation and trial, PW1 has given different versions of the incident.
At every stage, version of PW1 has improved and changed.
She has contradicted her earlier statement.
Her deposition before the Court suffers from material contradictions and inconsistencies which is not worthy of credence.
In these facts, testimony of complainant becomes unreliable and unworthy of credence.

31. Allegations under Section 509 IPC: Complainant also alleged that accuse persons abused her, but no specific words or attendance have been mentioned in the inheritance by the position by the complainant to show, which shows that she was abused by the accused persons with intent to indulge insult her modesty.
Hence the allegations against the accused persons are not proved for the offence punishable under section 509 IPC as well.

32. Hon'ble Apex Court in Balin Shahaja @ Shahajan Ismail Mohd. Shaikh Vs State of Maharashtra in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 883 has held as under:
SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
28.

sentences.text: To put it simply, in assessing the value of the evidence of the eyewitnesses, two principal considerations are whether, in the circumstances of the case, it is possible to believe their presence at the scene of occurrence or in such situations as would make it possible for them to witness the facts deposed to by them and secondly,
whether there is anything inherently improbable or unreliable in their evidence.

In respect of both these considerations, the circumstances either elicited from those witnesses themselves or established by other evidence tending to improbabilise their presence or to discredit the veracity of their statements, will have a bearing upon the value which a Court would attach to their evidence.

Although in cases where the plea of the accused is a mere denial, yet the evidence of the prosecution witnesses has to be examined on its own merits, where the accused raise a definite plea or puts forward a positive case which is inconsistent with that of the prosecution, the nature of such plea or case and the probabilities in respect of it will also have to be taken into account while assessing the value of the prosecution evidence.

33. In S.Govindaraju vs State Of Karnataka (2013) 15 SCC 315, Hon'ble Apex Court held:
It is well settled legal proposition that while appreciating the evidence, the court has to take into consideration whether the contradictions/omissions were of such magnitude so as to materially affect the trial.

entities.text: S.Govindaraju vs State Of Karnataka (2013) 15 SCC 315
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Minor contradictions, inconsistencies,
embellishments or improvements in relation to trivial matters, which do not effect the core of the case of the prosecution, must not be made a ground for rejection of evidence in its entirety.

The trial court, after going through the entire evidence available, must form an opinion about the credibility of the witnesses, and the appellate SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
State vs Shiv Lal Etc on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27293229/
8 court in the normal course of action, would not be justified in reviewing the same,
without providing justifiable reasons for doing so.

Where the omission(s) amount to a contradiction, creating a serious doubt regarding the truthfulness of a witness, and the other witnesses also make material improvements before the court in order to make the evidence acceptable, it would not be safe to rely upon such evidence.
The discrepancies in the evidence of eyewitnesses, if found not to be minor in nature, may be a ground for disbelieving and discrediting their evidence.

In such circumstances,
the witnesses may not inspire confidence and if their evidence is found to be in conflict and contradiction with other evidence available or with a statement that has already been recorded, then in such a case, it cannot be held that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.

34. Above discussed deposition of injured and eye witnesses, in view of inconsistency, variation and marked improvement does not inspire confidence specially when they have a motive to falsely implicate accused persons in view of the fact that a quarrel had taken place in which accused persons also sustained injuries.
From the discussions herein above, it emerges that testimony of complainant and his family members is marked improvement to their initial statements which renders their deposition untrustworthy.
Conclusion 35.
Accordingly, accused persons stands acquitted for the said charge.
Their personal bond is canceled and sureties are discharged.
Documents, if any, be returned to the surety.
SC No. 56077/2016 " State. v. Shiv Lal & Ors"
In terms of Section 437(A) Cr.P.C. Accused are directed to furnish personal & surety bond in the sum of Rs. 10,000/- for period of six months.
